channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Aluminium: Midwest premium to stay elevated – ING
item.description: ING Commodities Strategist Ewa Manthey analyses US aluminium policy and market structure, highlighting that Washington’s amended Section 232 tariffs aim to incentivize domestic smelting but will not quickly resolve the supply shortfall.

item.title: Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole dilemma: Say too much, too little, or just enough
item.description: Kevin Warsh is preparing to deliver his first Jackson Hole speech as Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair on Friday, and expectations extend well beyond whether interest rates will be raised or left unchanged in September.

item.title: Oil: Tight balance persists as Iran deal talk grows – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategists Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that heavy deal-related headlines around Iran and Oman are influencing energy markets, but they argue Crude Oil fundamentals remain tight.

item.title: Gold slips as sticky US PCE inflation fails to boost Fed rate-hike expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades around $4,620 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.83% on the day.

item.title: Euro comes under pressure against US Dollar after mixed US PCE data
item.description: EUR/USD trades under modest pressure on Wednesday after the US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index report delivered a mixed inflation picture.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade dispute risks weigh on Canada – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that Washington is considering further trade penalties against Canada after Ottawa’s dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new U.S. tariffs. Canada plans to double counter-tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum and add new duties on a range of goods.

item.title: Breaking: US core PCE inflation holds steady at 3.3% in July as expected
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, remained unchanged at 3.7% YoY in July, the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported on Wednesday. This reading came in above the market expectation of 3.6%.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Hot CPI supports carry and RBA risk – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports the Australian Dollar (AUD) is outperforming after hotter-than-expected July Consumer Price Index (CPI) data lifted Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) rate hike expectations.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Weakness before renewed strength – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank FX analyst Michael Pfister argues that the Swiss Franc (CHF) will stay under pressure through 2026 as markets gradually price out expectations of a Swiss National Bank (SNB) rate hike.

item.title: Euro holds upper hand against British Pound on diverging ECB-BoE expectations
item.description: EUR/GBP edges higher on Wednesday, though price action remains confined to the narrow range that has been in place since late July, largely between 0.8540 and 0.8580.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention impact assessed – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley reviews Japan’s FX intervention and its impact on USD/JPY.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer energy supports carry trades – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that lower Oil prices and the recent intervention by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have pushed long-end US yields 10–15bp lower, reducing FX and equities volatility.

item.title: Indian Rupee poised for positive opening on Thursday amid lower oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) is expected to open on a positive note against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after a holiday on Wednesday on account of Id-e-Milad. On Tuesday, the USD/INR pair declined 0.35% to near 95.40 due to weaker oil prices, which also led to a sharp decline in US Treasury Yields.

item.title: Euro: ECB tightening outlook offers support against US Dollar - BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu highlights that European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel sees further rate hikes as necessary, with Euro area inflation risks still tilted to the upside and growth more resilient than expected.

item.title: Japanese Yen treads water around 159.00 with US PCE Inflation on tap
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) ticks higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday but keeps looking for direction, as investors bide their time, awaiting an array of key US macroeconomic releases due later on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA tightening risks rise – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Prashant Newnaha highlights that Australia’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI delivered a strong inflation impulse, with headline and trimmed mean measures beating consensus and remaining uncomfortably high.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Range-bound consolidation as PCE looms – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is firm, consolidating just above recent lows following the US Treasury buyback announcement.

item.title: Gold slips ahead of US PCE as US Dollar firms modestly
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Wednesday as buyers trim their exposure ahead of the US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data, due at 12:30 GMT. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,615 after reaching $4,697 on Tuesday, its highest since May 14.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Hits fresh intra-week lows after failure at 1.3660 resistance
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) pares gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with bears testing the bottom of the intra-week trading range at the 1.3620 area, after failure to breach resistance at 1.3660.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Approaches 20-day EMA on the back of US-Canada trade dispute
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades 0.2% higher at around 1.3870 against the Canadian Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The Loonie pair strengthens as the Canadian Dollar underperforms due to trade tensions between the United States (US) and Canada.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD corrects to near $4,620 in countdown to US PCE Inflation data
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is down 0.75% to near $4,620 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike expectations support JPY against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes the Japanese Yen is firmer versus most G10 currencies as markets increasingly price a Bank of Japan rate hike in September.

item.title: WTI Oil drops below $80 amid hopes of Hormuz reopening, US-Iran de-escalation
item.description: Crude prices extend their reversal on Wednesday, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trading at the $79.50 area as of writing, highlighting a 9% decline from last week’s highs above $87.00.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Watching 0.7200 resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD extended its consolidation slightly higher, closing at 0.7165 as short-term momentum improves.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Recovery tied to euro entry story – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner reports that the National Bank of Hungary cut its policy rate by 25bp to 5.50%, with Chief Economist Peter Virovacz seeing a 4.75% terminal rate.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $68.54 per troy ounce, down 0.16% from the $68.65 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Range trade persists as data soft – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that the DXY Index’s recent recovery stalled slightly above 99 and has reverted to a 98.5–99.0 range after last week’s sell-off linked to higher US long bond yields.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests nine-day EMA confluence support near 185.00
item.description: EUR/JPY depreciates after registering modest gains, trading around 185.60 during the European hours on Wednesday. The technical analysis of a daily chart indicates that the currency cross is remaining within the ascending channel pattern, signaling an ongoing bullish bias.

item.title: Brent: Diplomatic progress weighs on prices – OCBC
item.description: OCBC Bank strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that improved prospects for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and diplomatic developments involving Iran and Oman have eased supply concerns, pushing Brent crude below USD90/bbl.

item.title: US Dollar: Shaky basis trade risks weigh – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur explains how the US Treasury Secretary’s vague secondary sanctions comments and falling US yields have left the Dollar stabilizing but vulnerable.
